transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm... just having a hard time lately. I can't really shake this feeling that work isn't... safe anymore. And I just feel kind of damaged now, I guess. Like the person I was, the one who was competent enough to get promoted... she isn't really there anymore.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately?
Um... no, I don't think so. Not... not depressed, anyway. Just... what I mentioned before. I just don't feel like myself.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge, especially at work?

I guess you could say that. I just... I can't really relax. Like on the train, or in meetings... even just at lunch with my team. I'm always automatically checking where the exits are, or... watching to see if someone is standing too close. I just keep an ear tuned to noises out in the hallway instead of... actually being present, I guess.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of something distressing, or because you feel unsafe?

Um... yeah, I suppose I have. I've been... working from home whenever I can. And when I do have to go in, I take the side entrance now. 

I just... I try to avoid walking through that main lobby after dark. It makes me feel like I'm... like I'm going to come apart, I guess. So I've been trading shifts, or... pushing back on our release windows, just to make sure I don't have to be there late.
Can you think of a specific event or situation at work—or elsewhere—that might be connected to how you're feeling now? Something that stands out as particularly unsettling or traumatic for you?

Um... yeah. There was... a break-in. It happened during an overnight deployment we were doing. That was about... two years and four months ago. I guess... everything has just been going on since then.
Have your symptoms, like feeling unsafe and avoiding certain places, been happening consistently since the break-in, or have they come and gone over time?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly... kept track of it. It just sort of feels like it's been this way for a while. I don't really know if it comes and goes.
Have you been feeling this way for more than a month, or is this something that has gotten worse recently?

Um... yeah, definitely more than a month. Like I just said, it's... it's been going on since the break-in. During that deployment two years and four months ago. So... yeah. It hasn't just been recent.
Do you ever find yourself reliving or re-experiencing the break-in—like having flashbacks, nightmares, or intrusive thoughts about it?

Um... yeah. Sometimes. Little things just... bring it back. Like if I hear a badge scanner beep, or... heavy footsteps out in the hall. Or if I get an alert for a late-night deployment. It just... suddenly I'm right back in that office. My chest gets all tight, and I just see the guard on the floor. It just cuts through whatever I'm trying to do.
Since the break-in, have you noticed that you're easily startled, or that you're constantly on guard, even in situations where there's no real danger?

Um... yeah. I guess I am. I just... I'm always watching things now. Like, on the train, or... in meetings. Even if I'm just at lunch with my team. I just... automatically clock the exits. I watch who's standing too close. I just keep one ear tuned to the hallway noises... instead of, you know, being fully present. So, yeah. I guess I'm on guard.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or thoughts about yourself since the break-in, such as feeling numb, detached, or having a sense that you're broken or damaged in some way?

Um... yeah. I guess so. I just... I can't really shake the feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And... I don't know, I just feel kind of... damaged, I guess. Like... the competent person who got promoted just... isn't really there anymore.

Since the break-in, have you found that your thoughts about yourself or your abilities have changed in a way that feels permanent, like you're not the same person anymore, or that you can't do things you used to handle easily?
Um... I don't know. I guess I already said I feel kind of damaged. I just... I don't really want to talk about it anymore than that.
Have your symptoms, like feeling unsafe and being on edge, been happening consistently since the break-in, or have they come and gone over time?

Um... yeah, it's... it's been pretty constant. Ever since that overnight deployment... when the break-in happened. That was... I don't know, about two years and four months ago now. It hasn't really stopped since then.

Do the symptoms you described—like feeling unsafe, being on edge, and reliving the event—only happen in relation to the break-in, or do they also occur in response to other stressful situations or events?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I don't think I've really noticed. It's mostly just... about that night, I guess. I haven't really paid attention to other stuff.
Do your symptoms—like feeling unsafe or on edge—only happen when you're reminded of the break-in, or do they also happen in other situations that aren't related to that night?
Um... I think you just asked me that. Like I said, I haven't really noticed. It's... it's just about the break-in. I don't know about other situations.
Do you ever feel unsafe or on edge even when you’re not thinking about the break-in, like in everyday situations that most people wouldn’t find threatening?

Um... well, yeah, I guess so. Even when I'm not thinking about it, I'm just... aware. Like on the train, or... in meetings at work. Even just at lunch with my team, I... I just automatically check where the exits are. I watch if people are standing too close to me. And I'm always... listening to the hallway noises, instead of just focusing on what's happening. So, yeah... I guess it happens then, too.

Have you noticed that situations similar to the break-in—like unexpected noises or being in enclosed spaces—trigger your symptoms more often, or do these symptoms now happen even in completely unrelated situations?

Um... I guess it's mostly certain noises. Like... if I hear a badge scanner beep, or... heavy footsteps in the hallway. Even just a late-night deployment alert. When that happens, it... it suddenly puts me right back in that office. My chest gets tight, and... I just see the image of the guard on the floor. It just cuts through whatever I'm doing. So... yeah, things like that.
